title: Inspector general found Lafayette Park clearing was planned for fence installation
description_short: Inspector general found Lafayette Park clearing was planned for fence installation
description_medium: An Interior Department inspector general review found that U.S. Park Police cleared Lafayette Park on June 1, 2020, to allow contractors to install anti-scale fencing. The report said the evidence did not support a finding that the park was cleared to enable President Trump’s walk to St. John’s Church. The operation ended at 6:50 p.m.; Trump entered the park at 7:01 p.m.
description_long: The Department of the Interior inspector general reviewed the U.S. Park Police operation at Lafayette Park on June 1, 2020. The report states that the evidence did not support a finding that Park Police cleared the park to let President Trump survey damage or walk to St. John’s Church. Instead, it found the stated operational purpose was to allow a contractor to safely install anti-scale fencing after property damage and officer injuries during earlier protests. The clearing operation ran from 6:23 to 6:50 p.m.; Trump walked through the park at 7:01 p.m. The report says the USPP began developing its plan hours before it learned of Trump’s potential movement; the contractor began assembling the fence at 7:30 p.m. This corrects the asserted photo-op motive while preserving the sequence. The review’s finding does not resolve every question about force, warnings, or individual actions by all participating agencies.

sources.support_note: The Department of the Interior OIG report supports the operational purpose (contractor installation of anti-scale fencing), the 6:23–6:50 p.m. clearing and 7:01 p.m. walk, that USPP began planning hours before learning of Trump’s potential movement, and that the contractor began assembling/installing fencing at 7:30 p.m. The report does not resolve every use-of-force question.
sources.uncertainty: This operational finding does not assess every use of force or resolve conduct by every agency or officer.

source_to_fact_mapping.support: The Department of the Interior OIG report supports the operational purpose (contractor installation of anti-scale fencing), the 6:23–6:50 p.m. clearing and 7:01 p.m. walk, that USPP began planning hours before learning of Trump’s potential movement, and that the contractor began assembling/installing fencing at 7:30 p.m. The report does not resolve every use-of-force question.

supported_facts: The OIG report says the evidence did not support that Park Police cleared Lafayette Park to enable Trump’s walk to St. John’s Church; it identifies contractor installation of anti-scale fencing as the operational purpose.
The operation ran from 6:23 to 6:50 p.m.; Trump walked through the park at 7:01 p.m.
The report says USPP began developing its plan hours before learning of Trump’s potential movement, and the contractor began assembling the fence at 7:30 p.m.
unsupported_original_claims: That the clearing was ordered specifically for a staged photo-op or Trump’s church visit.
That the entire crowd was peaceful; the OIG described prior property damage and officer injuries and does not support that blanket characterization.
Any claim that the OIG found no force concerns; its report separately noted warning audibility and other operational issues.
exact_evidence_gap: The OIG review does not determine the legality or appropriateness of every use of force by all agencies and officers; it does not support a blanket characterization that the entire crowd was peaceful or that all force concerns were resolved.
